x: The affair started O.K., as Ellis ran through a field of 35 and won the 880 from scratch in 1-59 on this terrible track, but the field was a very poor class except for about 5 "Birchfielders." Beman was on 50yds.

Our man's running gave the crowd a great thrill, for it gripped the imagination to see a young runner not yet 21 giving Hampson a keen tussle and making men like Gutteridge and Ellis look like "selling-platers."

Probably the best feat of the evening was that of Arthur Penny in winning the two miles run from scratch; whilst the performances of Don Brown in the Walk, Stroud in the 220 yards, and Ellis in the Shot Putt were very creditable.

Nowak as Vice-Captain, and with the assistance of enthusiasts like Clemens, Powell, Holder, Henchoz, Ivall, Kelly, Ellis, and others; and the addition of some newcomers, we may be certain that the Field Events men will contribute their share towards the progress the Club continues to make.

Bingham was about ten yards behind Cole and close to him followed two Northern men, Ellis and Tyrer. The second lap saw no change in the leading positions, but Reid had jumped ahead of Carter, who was running on his own some 15 yards from the Birchfielder.
We were unable to field a complete team and so our lads had to run as individuals. Ellis ran well for his first race.

Bill Lucas took the last leg and was unable to make much impression on the leader, Ellis of Aylesford, despite the fact that he ran the second fastest lap of the afternoon, and the Kent club were good winners by a margin of 24 seconds.
He did second fastest time, being a second faster than Ellis of Thames Valley, the actual winner, but for the first time since 1931 we found ourselves beaten out of a place.
Ellis of Maidenhead showed the way in the early stages with Chas. Walker going up to him but before very long Jack Brown and Ray Tooby had taken command.

At the change over S.L.H. were 75 seconds ahead of us and Jack Brown's course record of 28.21 had been beaten by Ellis, T.V.H. 28.20 who went through to 2nd, and by Llewellyn of Walton, 28.17 who took his club up seven places to 6th.

Dave Baulch ran well to hold our lead but on the next stage, Len Bishop had to give best to Ellis of T.V.H., and we were now second. A rather unhappy looking 'Jumbo' Masters, whom we welcomed back after a long absence, hung on to our position but we had slipped back on times.

Malcolm Robinson, our only entrant, found himself up against opponents such as Earl, Linford, Chapman and Ellis, but with his usual show of determination and ever-improving ability he secured a point with a time of 4m.2·4s., another best performance.

Ellis (TVH), had moved ahead of us; but the 'Hill' were our nearest rivals, 45 secs behind. The splendid run by Pat Newell gained us one place--that of TVH, but there were still 20 secs separating us from the Beagles; whilst Proffitt (Poly) and Llewellyn (Walton) were beyond capture.

Halton, Geoff finished second to Briault in the Sefton Brancker Trophy match between the Civil Service, Middlesex and the R.A.F In leading the Civil Service team to victory Geoff easily beat Price, Pugh, Presland, Barratt, Cooper, Ellis, Entwistle, Mellor, Lindsell and Holts.

Laurie O'Hara was immediately up with the leaders and only Ellis (TVH) and Lindsell (Ports) got the better of him. Pat Newell was next to run on the first of the short circuits (3½ miles) and soon overtook the Portsmouth runner (Plumpton) but Reading and Windsor were soon upon him and Pat had to be…
Despite the acquisition of Dai Davies the Welsh Champion, and fastest stage times by Wiggs and Ellis, our old rivals TVH could still only get within 47 seconds of us at the finish.

Trevor Hart knocked 17 secs off Pettit's lap record for the next stage to move us up to 2nd and a back-in-form Gerry North followed suit by lopping 24 secs off Ellis's record to put us way out in front.
John had the dubious pleasure of running solo knowing that Ellis (T.V.H.) Stevens (Reading) and Johnston (Portsmouth) were fighting it out behind.
